 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN M. DESAI  Date : 02/09/2025  ORAL ORDER 1.
The present application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for praying condonation of delay of 3605 days in preferring the first appeal.
2. Heard learned advocate Mr.Tejas Satta for the applicants - original claimants and learned AGP for the respondent - State.
Perused the record.

3. Learned advocate for the applicants submitted that the applicant's lands were acquired for the purpose NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined construction of Minsar irrigation project.

The award of Land Acquisition Officer was challenged by applicants by filing Reference cases being Land Reference Case No.94 of 2007 in group LAR Nos.82 Kansagara Bhikhubhai Odhavjibhai vs Deputy Collector on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138978716/
1 to 96 of 2007 before the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Khambhaliya at Jam Khambhaliya.

sentences.text: After considering the evidence by judgment and award dated 11.09.2014, learned Reference Court partly allowed the reference case.
3.1 It is further contended that the original claimant, who was handling the proceedings before the learned Reference Court and the legal heirs were not aware about such proceedings.

The legal heirs had no knowledge of the proceedings and when other claimants of the same group informed them about these proceedings, the legal heirs of the original claimant contacted the Advocate to take further steps in the matter.
Thus, the legal heirs are now on record in the proceedings before NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined this Court.
3.2 It is contended that a certified copy of the Award was applied for on 15.02.2023 and was delivered on 15.02.203.
The applicants are agriculturists and they are not able to understand the legal aspect.
3.3 The further submissions canvassed by learned advocate for the applicants are that due to Covid-19 Pandemic during the intervening period, there was a delay in challenging the impugned award.
There is no intentional delay on the part of the applicant and the object of the Act would be defeated, if the delay is not condoned.
Learned advocate for the applicants submitted that the applicants are ready and willing to waive and forgo interest for the delayed period on the enhanced compensation, if granted by this Court.

3.4 It is contended that by adopting a justice oriented view, the Hon'ble Supreme Court as well as NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined Hon'ble Division Bench and the Coordinate Bench of this Court, have condoned delays of more than 2000 days.
By condoning delay, applicants were directed not to claim interest for delayed period on enhanced amount, if awarded.
3.5 Learned advocate for the applicants has relied upon the following decisions:-

4. Per contra, learned AGP has vehemently objected and contended that, for condoning the delay for a huge period, the applicants must come up with a strong sufficient cause whereby a lenient view can be adopted by the Court.
In the present case, applicants have failed to explain the period of delay and has stated very general and vague grounds for condonation of delay.
It is submitted that the judgment and decree was passed in the year 2014 whereas the appeal is presented in the year 2024.

The contention raised by the applicants that they were not aware about the proceedings and came to know about the Reference Proceedings through other claimants, who were before the learned Reference Court along with the present applicant.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined 4.1

In support of the submissions, learned AGP has relied upon the following decisions:-
(i) Pathapati Subba Reddy (Died) By L.RS. And Ors.
Vs. Special Deputy Collector reported in 2024 Lawsuit(SC) 305,
(ii) Basawaraj and Anr. Vs. SPL Land Acquisition Officer reported in (2013) Lawsuit (SC) 739.

4.2 Except above, no other submissions are canvassed by learned AGP.
5.
Heard learned advocates for the respective parties and perused the papers placed on record.
It appears from record that the lands of the present applicants were acquired for the purpose of construction of Minsar irrigation project.
The Notification under Sections 4 and 6 of the Act was published on 10.05.2005 and 23.11.2005 respectively.
The award came to be challenged by the land owners before the learned Reference Court.

The learned Reference Court after considering the evidence NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined on record partly allowed Reference case.
6.

It appears form the record that the reason assigned in the application is that applicants were not aware about the reference proceedings and only came to know about from other claimants, who were handling the proceedings.
It also appears from the record that an application for a certified copy of the impugned award was applied by applicants, period of limitation to challenge the award had already expired.
The applicants have not been able to explained the yawning gap between the date of award and the application for certified copies of the award.
Even after gathering a knowledge that the adjoining villager had been awarded higher compensation, no such attempt was made by claimants to challenge the impugned award.
The applicants must explain as to when they came to know about the reference proceedings has been concluded.

A contention that the claimants knew NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined about the reference proceedings being concluded through other person who was handling the proceedings is vague.
It is not worth believing the explanation that the applicants were not aware about the proceedings initiated by them before the learned Reference Court for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: This Court is fully conscious about the fact that poor and illiterate litigants are not very much well-versed in furnishing necessary details to their learned advocates while drafting applications.

However, when the applicants are facing huge period of delay, they must provide strong and convincing explanations as to why the appeal was not filed within a reasonable time after knowing the conclusion of proceedings.
Conveniently applicants have suppressed the date of knowledge about the conclusion of reference proceedings.

The applicants have conveniently not stated as to when the compensation was deposited by NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED:
02/09/2025 undefined the acquiring body and when it was received by Claimants.
By making vague and general statements, applicants cannot plead that the reasons and explanations which are stated in the application are sufficient cause.
Applicant must establish that circumstances beyond their control prevented them from challenging the impugned award.

The cause which has been pitched of COVID-19 situation is an eye wash explanation for the reason that the impugned award was passed and when the COVID-19 pandemic condition worsened in the entire country resulting into a nationwide lockdown in the month of March 2020, period of limitation to file an appeal had already expired.
Applicants have not provided a single cogent reason, explaining the gap between the date of pronouncement of the award and March 2020.

Even, the cause attributed regarding knowledge that land owners of adjoining village were awarded higher compensation by NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined learned Reference Court, also establish fact that the applicants remained fence-sitter and remained negligent.
Even after knowing the award passed in adjoining village, certified copy of the impugned award was applied much thereafter.
The conduct of the applicants is such that lenient view cannot be adopted.
The applicants cannot be permitted to reopen a concluded case after unexplained sufficient cause of delay.
7. "Sufficient cause" means that the party should not have acted in a negligent manner or there was want of bona fide on its part in view of the facts and circumstances of a case.

The facts and circumstances of each case must afford sufficient ground to enable the Court concerned to exercise discretion for the reason that whenever the Court exercised discretion it has to be exercised judicially.

The applicant/s must satisfy the Court that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined prosecuting his case and unless a satisfactory explanation is furnished the Court should not allow the application for condonation of delay.

8. In the case of Imrat Lal (supra), on perusal of para 8 of the decision, it appears that the claimant pleaded sufficient cause as no details were disclosed by claimants to whom they had entrusted the task of filling an appeal.
Thus, it appears that the explanation for delay is non-filing of the appeal was as the person who was instructed to file appeal did not file the appeal within the prescribed period of limitation.

In background of aforesaid explanation, the Hon'ble Apex Court adopted a lenient view and upon the statement made by learned Senior Additional Advocate General that instead of remanding the matters to the High Court for consideration of appeal filed by the appellant under Section 54 of the Act, Court may grant relief to them in terms of judgement, passed in NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined Sudama versus State of Haryana and connected matters.
Therefore, in my view, the decision is not helpful to the applicants.

sentences.text: In the case of Sureshkumar (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court while considering delay in filing First Appeal, taken into consideration the ground for delay.
The ground taken by the appellant was that the documents had been given to the concerned person to file an appeal against the order of Reference Court, but the same was not filed.

The Apex Court had also taken into consideration the decision in the case of Dhiraj Singh Vs. State of Haryana & Others and a decision in the case of Huchanagouda Vs. Assistant Commissioner and Land Acquisition Officer and Anr.

sentences.text: Considering the reason, which was found to be a sufficient cause for condoning delay, a justice oriented view was adopted and delay was condoned.
In the present case, the grounds stated in the NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined application are too vague to be considered as a sufficient cause for condoning delay.

In every application for condonation of delay, the length of delay is not only the sole criteria in judging whether explanation, canvassed falls within a sufficient cause, but the explanations which are canvassed to be judged whether they are sufficient cause or not.

10. In the background of the explanations which are tendered by applicants, the decisions relied upon by the applicants in the case of Suresh Kumar (Supra) and case of Huchanagouda (supra), are not helpful to the applicants.
11. In the case of Ningappa (supra), claimants sought parity with other ex appropriated land owners.
The State assailed the award of reference Court.
The High Court allowed the appeals of State.

The decision of High Court was assailed by some of the landowners by way of Special Leave Petition before the Hon'ble Apex Court and NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED:
02/09/2025 undefined the Hon'ble Apex Court allowed the Appeal and set aside the order of High Court and restored the award of Reference Court.
The applicants did not assail the order of High Court & after a period of huge delay approached Hon'ble Apex Court by way of Special Leave Petition and sought Parity.
In the present case, such as naughty explanations for causing delay.
Therefore, in my view the aforesaid decision is not helpful to the applicant.
12. In the case of K.Subbarayudu (supra), the explanation which was placed by applicants was that they were under the impression that an appeal had been filed.
However, upon enquiry, they learnt that the Advocate entrusted with the task of filing the appeal, was no more and expired and no appeal was filed.

All the decisions which have been relied upon by applicants are perused, the applicants could satisfy the Court that there were NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined sufficient causes or the circumstances were beyond their control resultantly, there was a delay in challenging the impugned award.

Keeping in mind the explanation,
the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Subbarayudu (supra), condoned the delay with a condition that the applicants shall not be entitled interest on additional compensation.

13. It would be profitable to refer and rely upon the decision passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of The State of Gujarat & Ors Vs. Dahayabhai Nyalchand Vora reported in (2014)SCC Online Guj 6805.

In paragraph No.6, this Court has observed as under:-

5 "6.

sentences.text: Turning to the explanation offered in the present case, in light of the above parameters set by the Apex Court, it was conspicuously noticed that judgment sought to be challenged was delivered on 14 th October, 2011, however the certified copy was applied after moire than six months.
In other words, even the certified copy was not applied within the period of limitation.
The limitation had already expired when the Departmental realised that certified copy was not available and the same was required to be obtained.
When the telegram was sent by officer concerned for applying certified copy, the papers had reached Government Pleader's office for drafting and actual filing.
The officers of the Department cannot disclaim the knowledge of proceedings, requirements and in particular the period of limitation within which, the appeal could be required to be preferred.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined 6.1

In Office of the Chief Post Master General(supra), it was appropriately observed by the Apex Court that the persons concerned were well aware or conversant with the issues involved including the prescribed period of limitation for taking up the matter before the higher court.
In that case the certified copy of the High Court's judgment was applied for only after four months by the Postal Department, who had preferred SLP before the Supreme Court.
6.2 It may be true that in a given or special case, late applying of certified copy may have good reason to be condoned.

But, ordinarily and in all normal cases, the act of applying certified copy immediately or at least within the period of limitation after deliverance of the judgment proposed to be challenged,
is an important measure of litigant's vigilance.
It is also a reflection of intention to carry the case in appeal and agitate for his rights.
This much amount of vigilance is expected, whether it is a private individual or a government department.

Therefore,
without making a rule of thumb, it can be safely stated that when the certified copy is not applied within the period of limitation, it suggests apathy and negligence on part of the litigant.
In the present case, there is no explanation for time gap between 14th October, 2011 and 21st April, 2012.

Given this conduct of not applying the certified copy till the papers reached the office of the Government Pleader at High Court, the explanation about time taken in exhausting different decisional stages turned out to be the lame excuse, judicially not acceptable.

Mere movement of files from one table to another and the stock ground of administrative procedure cannot furnish a good cause and a sufficient cause in all cases, unless the time consumed in the decision making process is shown to be bonafide.

6.3 Indolence on part of the applicants in the matter of preferring Appeal is further reinforced in view of uncontroverted fact that in the afore-mentioned writ petition filed by the respondent herein, certified copy of the judgment of the District Court sought to be impugned in the Second Appeal was placed on record of that petition as back as in December, 2011.
The applicants herein who were respondents in the writ petition, were thus posted with knowledge.
They were aware, yet they did not act in the matter.
It was only after eight months that in July, 2012, Appeal and delay condonation Application was filed.

The unexplained yawning gap between the date of judgment and applying of certified copy and the aforesaid aspect, is indicative of gross apathy and indolence on part of Kansagara Bhikhubhai Odhavjibhai vs Deputy Collector on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138978716/
6 the applicants and its officers."

sentences.text: In the case of Baswaraj and another (Supra), which has been referred by the Hon'ble Apex Court in paragraph No.23, a law has been laid down that expression 'sufficient cause' as occurred in Section 5 of Limitation Act cannot be liberally interpreted if negligence, inaction or lack of bonafide is writ large.
16. In paragraph No.26, the Hon'ble Apex Court has interpreted what is sufficient cause in condoning delay.

sentences.text:
In paragraph 30, the Hon'ble Apex Court observed as under:
"30.
The aforesaid decisions would not cut any ice as the imposition of conditions is not warranted when sufficient cause has not been shown for condoning the delay.
Secondly,delay is not liable to be condoned merely because some persons have been granted relief on the facts of their own case.
Condonation of delay in such circumstances is in violation of the legislative intent and express provision of the statute.

Condoning the delay merely for the reason that the claimants have been deprived of the interest for the delay, without holding that they had made out a case for condoning the delay, is not a correct approach, particularly when both the above decisions have been rendered in ignorance of the earlier pronouncement in the case of Basawaraj (supra).
19.

The contention of learned advocate for the applicants that the applicants can be saddled with a cost of waiving of interest on the enhanced amount, in paragraph No.31, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under :
"31.

Learned counsel for the petitioners next submitted, on the basis of additional documents, that in connection with the land acquisition in some other Special Leave Petitions, delay was condoned by taking a lenient view and compensation was enhanced with the rider that the claimants shall not be entitled for statutory benefits for the period of delay in approaching this Court or the High Court.

The said orders do not clearly spell out the facts and reasons explaining the delay in filing the appeal(s), but the fact remains that the delay was condoned by taking too liberal an approach and putting conditions which have not been approved by this Court itself.

In the absence of clear facts justifying condonation of delay in NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/243/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/09/2025 undefined the referred cases,
vis--vis the facts of the present case, it cannot be said that the reasons for condoning the delay are identical or similar.

Therefore, we are unable to exercise our discretionary power of condoning the delay in filing the appeal on parity with the Kansagara Bhikhubhai Odhavjibhai vs Deputy Collector on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138978716/
8

20. Considering the averments made in the application and submissions of the learned advocates for the parties, I am of the view that the applicants are not bonafide litigants and no convincing and palatable explanation forthcoming for allowing the present application of condonation of delay.
Considering the overall aspects and conduct of applicants cannot be viewed as a bonafide mistake or lapse, therefore, present application is dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
No order as to costs.
